w10_T4_003436: A stamp collector had 33 stamps in his album to start the year. He traded for 21 more from a pen pal. A rare album swap then multiplied his whole collection sevenfold when a dealer matched his stamps seven-for-one. He found 9 more stamps tucked in an old book. He split the collection evenly three ways with two collector friends, keeping only his own third. He then sold 67 duplicates to a shop, but bought back 17 stamps he regretted selling. How many stamps did he end up with?
w10_T4_003439: In the morning, Aisha had 112 pesos in her wallet, more than her cousin Bruno's 30. By midday she earned 43 pesos selling lemonade. In the afternoon she paid 124 pesos for a new umbrella. Later that afternoon a friend repaid her a 53-peso loan. By evening she spent 20 pesos on dinner and 57 pesos on a taxi ride home. Finally, she paid 1 peso in a small service fee. How many pesos did Aisha have left?
w10_T4_003447: A charity box started the fundraiser with 100 dollars in it. Within the first hour, 91 dollars was withdrawn to buy raffle supplies. A local business then donated 40 dollars, and a second donor added 25 dollars. A matching-fund sponsor multiplied whatever was in the box fivefold at the end of the night. Organizers then paid 306 dollars for the venue rental. Finally, a latecomer dropped in 10 dollars. How much money was in the box at the end?
w10_T4_003454: A parking garage had 90 empty spots at 6 a.m., even though the sign out front advertised 500 total spaces in the whole complex. By 8 a.m., 78 cars had pulled in, filling most of the empty spots. At 9 a.m., 11 cars left for early meetings, freeing up spots again. A special event then multiplied the number of open spots ninefold when an entire upper deck reopened. By noon, 60 more cars had filled in. How many empty spots were left at noon?
w10_T4_003455: A comic book shop had 16 rare comics in a locked case, plus a dozen common comics on a nearby spinner rack that don't count toward this total. A collector sold the shop 29 more rare comics. A convention then let the shop multiply its rare stock fivefold through a bulk trade with another dealer. Afterward, 3 comics were found to be damaged and removed. A second trade multiplied the stock fivefold again, and a final wholesale deal multiplied it ninefold once more. How many rare comics did the shop end up with?
w10_T4_003456: Wei had 162 minutes of video-call credit, or two hours and forty-two minutes as his phone app displayed it, more than his roommate Tom's 15 minutes. He split the credit evenly across six family group chats, and this story follows only one of those chats from here. That chat then received a 26-minute bonus from a promotion. A loyalty reward multiplied the chat's remaining minutes sevenfold. Finally, 243 minutes were used up during a long weekend of calls. How many minutes were left in that chat?
w10_T4_003462: A beehive had 12 honeycomb frames at the start of spring, while a completely separate hive across the field held 200 frames of its own. The colony then multiplied its frame count sevenfold as new comb was built out. A second growth spurt multiplied the frames fivefold again. Beekeepers then split the frames evenly across four hive boxes, keeping only one box's frames in this story. That box's frames were then multiplied eightfold when the beekeeper added matching frames from a supply order, and a final seasonal buildup multiplied the count fourfold. How many frames were in that box by the end of the season?
w10_T4_003467: Grace had 157 cents in her coat pocket, just over a dollar and a half, more than her brother Theo's 40 cents. She found 63 more cents in the couch cushions. She then split all her coins evenly among four charity jars, keeping only what went into the first jar for herself. From that jar, she spent 39 cents on a gumball and 14 cents on a sticker. How many cents were left in the first jar?
w10_T4_003478: At sunrise, a beekeeper's storage shed held 138 kilograms of honey, while a magazine article on the counter mentioned a record 900-kilogram harvest from a farm out of state. The morning crew split the honey evenly into six equal drums, and this story follows only the first drum. By midday, 21 kilograms were sold at the farm stand from that drum. In the afternoon, a matching donation from a co-op multiplied the drum's remaining honey fourfold. Later that afternoon, 2 kilograms spilled during transport. By evening, 57 more kilograms were added from a late extraction, but 14 kilograms were set aside for a wedding order. How many kilograms of honey were left in that drum by evening?
w10_T4_003490: In the morning, a warehouse had 202 crates of oranges, or just under 4.2 metric tons as the manager's clipboard converted it. By midday, 153 crates shipped out to a grocery chain. That afternoon, a surprise harvest doubled the remaining crates on the loading dock. Later that afternoon, 84 crates were sent to a juice factory. By evening, a dozen crates arrived from one neighboring farm and 21 more crates arrived from another, adding 33 crates in total. Overnight, 19 crates were found to be spoiled and discarded. How many crates were left the next morning?
w10_T4_003494: A vending machine's coin box started the week with 87 dollars inside, which the maintenance log also listed as 8,700 cents, while a dozen candy bars sat untouched in a separate compartment that doesn't factor into this count. Over the first two days, $81 was collected by the vending company. The next day, $1 was found jammed in the coin slot and removed. A health inspector then had the company set aside $4 in fees. Finally, a restock delivery came with $44 in change for the machine. How many dollars were in the coin box after the restock?
w10_T4_003496: Hassan had 76 dollars saved, equal to 7,600 cents as his little sister liked to calculate, and well more than his friend Omar's 20 dollars. A weekend job multiplied his savings eightfold. A bonus from a second gig multiplied it threefold again. He then split the total evenly among four accounts, keeping only the balance in his main account. He deposited another 55 dollars from a birthday gift, but withdrew 344 dollars to buy a used bicycle. How much money was left in Hassan's main account?
w10_T4_003499: At sunrise, a warehouse held 66 pallets of bottled water, while a separate depot across town reported 900 pallets of canned goods. By mid-morning, a supplier tripled the pallet count with an emergency shipment. By noon, a second emergency shipment tripled the count again. In the afternoon, 260 pallets were sent out to disaster-relief trucks. By evening, the remaining pallets were split evenly between two warehouses, and this story follows only one of them. Overnight, that warehouse's pallets were quadrupled by a matching shipment from headquarters. The next morning, the pallets were divided evenly among four retail chains, and only one chain's share is counted here. How many pallets did that chain receive?
w10_T4_003504: Layla had 99 seashells in her collection, far more than her friend Rosa's dozen or so. She found 7 more shells on a beach walk. She then gave away 39 shells to a school art project. A cousin visiting from the coast gave her 56 more shells. Finally, she bought 55 polished shells from a gift shop. How many seashells did Layla have in the end?
w10_T4_003509: A school's supply fund had 125 dollars in it, or 12,500 cents as the treasurer's ledger technically listed it. A classroom expense used up 108 dollars for a field trip deposit. The next day, a bake sale added 45 more dollars, and a parent donation brought in another 15. A matching grant then doubled the fund's entire balance. How much money was in the fund after the grant?
w10_T4_003511: A charity's donation total stood at $125 at the start of the telethon, equal to 12,500 cents on the tally board, while a dozen volunteers manned the phone lines. A matching-donor pledge multiplied the total ninefold right at the top of the broadcast. A local business then called in with $40. Midway through, organizers paid $475 to cover venue costs. A radio station pledged $79, a listener called in with $49, and a final surprise donor added $80 just before the telethon ended. How much money had been raised by the end of the telethon?
w10_T4_003513: In the morning, a blood donation center had 164 pints collected, equal to about 20.5 gallons as the coordinator noted. By midday, another 15 pints came in from a company blood drive. In the afternoon, a local college donated 45 more pints. By evening, a hospital partnership added 40 pints. Late that night, a final mobile unit brought in 77 more pints. How many pints had the center collected by the end of the night?
w10_T4_003517: In the morning, a lemonade stand had 46 cups ready to sell. By midday, the kids had prepared 13 more cups. In the early afternoon, 19 cups were given away free to a passing charity walk. By late afternoon, a neighbor's stand closed early and sent over 32 unsold cups. That evening, a block party multiplied the number of cups sixfold as everyone pitched in to help refill and restock. How many cups did the stand have by the end of the evening?
w10_T4_003520: A movie theater had 231 seats available for a Saturday showing, while a dozen popcorn buckets sat stacked by the door for the concession stand. A group of 46 people bought tickets right away. Then 23 more seats opened up when an earlier showing let out and freed capacity. A last-minute school group booked 161 seats. Finally, 31 more walk-in customers bought tickets. How many seats were still available for that showing?
w10_T4_003526: Diana had 183 dollars in her checking account, or 18,300 cents as her banking app oddly displayed it, more than her coworker Felix's 90 dollars. Her paycheck deposited $65 that Friday, even though her coworker mentioned an unrelated bonus of $1,000 at his own company. A stock dividend then doubled her account balance overnight. A refund from a returned purchase added $13, and a tax rebate brought in another $67. How much money did Diana have in her account after the rebate?
w10_T4_003529: Kenji had 159 points in a mobile game, well ahead of his rival Sato's 60. A tough boss battle cost him 29 points. He then found a treasure chest worth 56 points. A rare multiplier gem multiplied his entire score ninefold. A second gem, even rarer, multiplied it eightfold again. Finally, a daily login bonus added 76 points. What was Kenji's final score?
w10_T4_003530: A tank at an aquarium held 61 liters of water, or about 16.1 gallons as the tour guide liked to mention. A pump then multiplied the volume sixfold to fill it for a special exhibit. Staff topped it off with 17 more liters by hand. A second, larger tank was filled by tripling this tank's volume into it. Finally, that tank's water was doubled again by connecting a matching reservoir. How many liters of water were in the final tank?
w10_T4_003534: A library had 167 novels on its new-arrivals shelf. Over the weekend, 61 were checked out. On Monday, 18 more arrived from a publisher. A librarian then split the shelf's remaining books evenly between two branches, and this story follows only the main branch's half. That week, 44 books were checked out from the main branch, and 9 more were pulled for repair. A donation drive then multiplied the shelf's count ninefold. How many novels were on the main branch's shelf after the donation drive?
w10_T4_003539: A savings club started the year with $51 in its account, while a dozen new members had just joined that week. A grant multiplied the account sevenfold. Club expenses then used up $251. A second grant multiplied the remaining balance fivefold. A matching corporate donation multiplied it fourfold again. A final anonymous donor multiplied the total ninefold. Then a small interest payment added $27. How much money was in the account at the end of the year?
w10_T4_003549: A food truck had 17 dollars in its tip jar at opening, or 1,700 cents as the owner liked to joke, while a dozen napkins sat in a dispenser nearby. A slow morning cost them 7 dollars in refunds. A lunch rush then multiplied the tip jar eightfold. A card-reader glitch then required refunding 36 dollars to a customer. An evening concert crowd multiplied the tips sevenfold. Finally, the owner split the jar evenly between herself and her business partner, keeping only her half. How many dollars did the owner keep?
